At 10% progress, prioritize a fixed-weight, support-protected recent transition residual. No improvement has been measured; retain objective changes as a controlled alternative.

**Insights and directions.** Three starting-point insights motivate evidence-based fusion. (1) Directed transitions offer specific follow-on evidence, without establishing compatibility. (2) Recent anchors target excessive historical-interest influence, without identifying current intent. (3) Sparse transitions require explicit support protection: popularity-centered smoothing alone can favor rare singleton destinations.

Three literature insights refine the directions. (1) TGCL4SR motivates complementary sequence/transition evidence, not this residual’s effectiveness. (2) Dirichlet smoothing regularizes probabilities, but single-row log-lift still ranks by c_ij/q_j before clipping; clipping does not establish reliability. (3) gSASRec motivates objective controls; Cawley–Talbot cautions that repeated validation selection creates optimism. Embedding concentration near 0.5 does not justify a collapse-focused intervention.

**Framework and candidate assessment.** Directions remain transition evidence, adaptive temporal fusion, and ranking objectives. O/P/U/M/D denote originality, potential, user alignment, model alignment, and implementation difficulty, each 0–10; higher D means harder. Scores are prospective.

| Idea | O/P/U/M/D | Positive and negative assessment |
|---|---|---|
| Support-protected recent transition residual | 4/7/8/7/5 | O: useful synthesis, established ingredients; P: extensible evidence channel, sparse coverage; U: targets specificity and recency, cannot identify fulfilled needs; M: may repair wrong pairs, may introduce errors; D: sparse counting is simple, provenance and deployment parity require care. |
| Support-aware recent-history gate | 5/7/8/7/6 | O: combines timing/support, familiar gating; P: adaptive fusion, overfitting risk; U: emphasizes recent interests, intent remains latent; M: may protect weak rows, uncertain calibration; D: small network, OOF fitting adds complexity. |
| Uniform multi-negative cross-entropy | 3/7/4/8/4 | O: established objective, limited novelty; P: useful baseline, dataset-dependent gains; U: sharper rankings, weak recency mechanism; M: targets separation, uncertain negatives remain; D: unchanged encoder, careful sampling required. |

**Selected algorithm.** Persist three user-grouped folds per category before expanding examples. In each excluded-fold table, count adjacent transitions once per distinct contributing user per ordered pair; derive a positive destination prior from retained training interactions. Set p_ij=(c_ij+αq_j)/(n_i+α). Use r_ij=1[c_ij≥2]·min(3,max(0,log(p_ij/q_j))). This support threshold is a heuristic, not calibrated uncertainty. Average r over the last K prefix items using normalized weights 2^(−distance), then add λ times the result to SASRec scores. All transforms are candidate-independent; absent evidence contributes zero.

The mechanism targets broad matches displacing specific choices and historical interests outweighing recent intent. It targets wrong-pair rankings, especially Electronics/CDs, without claiming redundancy detection.

```python
folds = persist_grouped_user_folds(seed=0, n_folds=3)
tables = build_excluded_fold_support(training_histories, folds)
anchors = recent_prefix_items(sequence, endpoint=t, K=3)
scores = base_scores + weight * supported_lift(anchors, candidates, tables[user_fold])
```

Freeze α=10 and λ∈{0,0.25,1}; compare baseline BCE and fixed 32-negative CE, each with identical fusion. Preserve baseline checkpoint rules and count every selection decision. Cache validation scores with IDs/provenance; select only by four-category macro HR@10. Report paired stratified-bootstrap differences and discordant hits as exploratory after selection. Retain fold-excluded deployment tables and routing; do not silently rebuild all-user support. Diagnose with provenance-bearing prefix examples, preserving the anonymous four-tuple adapter contract. Preserve seeds, routing, DATA_DIR, artifact paths, and predictor-writer parity. Sampled-negative validation gains do not establish full-catalog or online gains.

idea.description: Add a fixed-weight, support-protected recent directed-transition residual to each category's SASRec. Use distinct-user transition counts, a positive popularity prior, clipped positive log-lift, and persistent excluded-fold tables. Compare this addition under both unchanged BCE and one fixed multi-negative CE objective.
idea.motivation: Recent directed evidence explicitly addresses two observed user-facing failures: broad associations displacing specific follow-ons, and historical interests outweighing recent behavior. It also offers a controlled intervention for the high supplied training-pair error rates in Electronics and CDs_and_Vinyl, 15.04% and 13.32%. These observations do not establish why errors occur or predict validation gains. The proposal does not infer compatibility, redundancy, ownership, unmet need, or simulator traits.
idea.implementation_notes:
Preserve all four category models and dataset routing, preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, DATA_DIR=os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], single-GPU execution, trial-local artifacts, and SASREC_EPOCHS default 200. Do not change benchmark splits, candidates, evaluation seed, or host evaluator. Use only training interactions, available titles/descriptions if separately ablated, and observed timestamps; the proposed residual needs only histories. Ratings, reviews, item categories, prices, stores, specifications, and simulator traits remain unavailable.

Persist three approximately balanced user folds per category using a deterministic seed-0 permutation of sorted training user IDs followed by round-robin assignment. Store category/user IDs, fold assignments, table versions, catalog mapping, and configuration. A user's entire history belongs to one fold. For each excluded-fold table, count an ordered adjacent pair at most once per contributing user, excluding padding and self-transitions; n_i is the sum of these distinct-user pair counts, not the number of distinct source users. Define q_j=(f_j+1)/(sum_k f_k+N), where f_j counts retained training interactions and N is the nonpadding catalog size. This deliberately combines user-supported edges with an interaction-frequency background; it is an association heuristic, not a calibrated generative model.

Fix alpha=10, minimum distinct-user edge support=2, positive log-lift cap=3, K=3, and normalized recency weights proportional to 2^(-distance), with distance zero for the newest nonpadding item. Unsupported edges and empty histories contribute zero. Before clipping, log-lift equals log(1+c_ij/(alpha*q_j))+log(alpha/(n_i+alpha)); smoothing cannot repair within-row singleton rankings. The threshold explicitly blocks singleton evidence, although two-user edges can still be unreliable. Positive clipping avoids broadly penalizing unseen transitions, but may overreward popular supported patterns. No statistical confidence interpretation is claimed.

Prespecify two neural runs per category: unchanged baseline BCE and uniform 32-negative sampled CE, with identical encoder, optimizer, training schedule, and baseline checkpoint-selection rule. For CE, use one positive and 32 distinct negatives per valid position; exclude padding, the target, and all known training-history items for that user without consulting held-out labels. Uniform sampling without replacement uses a per-example eligible pool; use all eligible negatives if fewer than 32 exist, and skip a position if none exist. Compute ordinary CE over the positive and sampled negatives without claiming an unbiased full-softmax approximation. This is a fixed objective control, not gBCE or a sampling-corrected estimator.

For each frozen neural checkpoint, evaluate lambda in {0,0.25,1}, producing six prespecified configurations. If compute limits prevent both objective runs from completing for every category, report the incomplete comparison rather than substituting categories or claiming the factorial experiment was completed. Keep total training, diagnostics, failed trials, and debugging within the shared 43,200 GPU-second budget. Preserve baseline checkpoint rules exactly and log their selection opportunities; fusion selection uses only the unchanged four-category macro validation HR@10. Freeze the grid and trial count before observing results. Cache component scores, user/candidate IDs, checkpoint provenance, and table versions when the evaluator exposes them, without modifying its scoring procedure. Cheap grid evaluation still creates selection opportunities.

Retain the three excluded-fold tables at inference, routing every known user through the persisted fold exclusion. Resolve the exact benchmark user identity from its input record and persisted preprocessing map; never infer identity from sequence content. If the prediction interface does not expose user identity, use a fixed category-specific fold for every request in both validation and deployment and report this variant explicitly; user-fold OOF diagnostic claims then require a separate provenance-bearing dataset and do not describe deployed routing. Previously unseen users use the same fixed category-specific fold. Fix these routing semantics before validation. Do not silently rebuild tables from all users or average folds, because either changes support and score semantics. Serialize the selected model, sparse tables, identities/routing where available, and fusion configuration; update the predictor writer so working/predict.py implements exactly the validated route and scoring.

Preserve DiagnosisProbe(view, device).run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), returning metrics and metric_definitions, and keep view.model as the actual trained nn.Module. Preserve item_emb, log2feats, predict_score, user_train, meta_data, and review_data compatibility. Make log2feats return an explicitly documented feature layout containing neural features and the current prefix's recent item IDs; it must not include future positions. Provide view.predict_score_base. Anonymous train_loader batches cannot establish user ownership. Generate an additional deterministic diagnostic stream directly from view.user_train, retaining category, user ID, prefix endpoint, example ID, and fold; compare residual-on/off scores on identical positive/negative candidates using the appropriate excluded-fold table. Keep anonymous-batch neural diagnostics separate. If provenance or valid paired candidates are unavailable, mark fold-dependent comparisons unavailable. Preserve the distinction between OOF training diagnostics and deployed routing; never recover identity by matching truncated histories.

Report paired corrections and regressions, per-category hit changes, discordant validation hit counts, and macro improvement. If per-user validation hits are available through permitted evaluator outputs, run 10,000 paired bootstrap replicates with RNG seed 42, independently resampling users within each category and averaging category differences equally; report the percentile 95% interval. Otherwise report that this interval is unavailable rather than modifying the evaluator. Winner intervals are exploratory and conditional on frozen models and candidates; they omit training-seed variability, negative-sampling variability, and selection bias. Avoid confirmatory significance claims. The benchmark measures HR@10 against 99 sampled negatives; full-catalog simulator recommendations remain a separate qualitative assessment for the prescribed twenty real training users. User grouping does not establish global chronological causality, and no chronology changes to the pinned splits are proposed.

Defer learned gating, Bayesian posterior thresholds, Markov-probability fusion, sequential rules, and V-SKNN to separately budgeted work. They are useful alternatives, but adding them to this early-stage selection grid would increase compute and validation-selection exposure. Bayesian uncertainty would require handling estimated-background uncertainty and repeated-user dependence rather than treating a Beta approximation as calibrated evidence.
idea.pseudocode:
CONFIG = {folds: 3, alpha: 10.0, min_users: 2, cap: 3.0,
          recent_K: 3, lambdas: [0.0, 0.25, 1.0], negatives: 32}

# All inputs below are public training histories; preserve benchmark splits.
fold_map = seed0_balanced_user_folds(sorted_user_ids, CONFIG.folds)
persist(fold_map, catalog_mapping, CONFIG)

for fold in range(CONFIG.folds):
    retained = users_outside_fold(training_users, fold_map, fold)
    counts = sparse_counts()
    frequency = zeros(nonpadding_catalog_size)
    for user in retained:
        history = training_history[user]
        frequency += item_frequencies(history)
        pairs = set((a, b) for a, b in adjacent(history)
                    if a != 0 and b != 0 and a != b)
        for a, b in pairs:
            counts[a, b] += 1
    q = (frequency + 1) / (sum(frequency) + catalog_size)
    tables[fold] = (counts, row_sums(counts), q)

# Set identity/routing capability once, before validation.
def route(category, public_user_id):
    if identity_is_available and public_user_id in saved_fold_map[category]:
        return saved_fold_map[category][public_user_id]
    return saved_fixed_fold[category]

def residual(prefix, candidates, table):
    counts, totals, q = table
    anchors = last_nonpadding(prefix, K=3)
    if not anchors:
        return zeros_like_candidates(candidates)
    weights = normalize([2 ** (-distance) for distance in distances_from_newest(anchors)])
    result = zeros_like_candidates(candidates)
    for item, weight in zip(anchors, weights):
        c = counts[item, candidates]
        p = (c + 10.0 * q[candidates]) / (totals[item] + 10.0)
        evidence = where(c >= 2, clamp(log(p / q[candidates]), 0, 3), 0)
        result += weight * evidence
    return result

# At training position t, use only sequence[:t+1], predicting positive[t].
# Diagnostics obtain user/fold provenance directly from user_train, not anonymous batches.
for objective in ['baseline_BCE', 'uniform_32_negative_CE']:
    models = train_all_four_categories(seed=42, objective=objective,
                                       checkpoint_rule=unchanged_baseline_rule)
    for weight in [0.0, 0.25, 1.0]:
        score = base_score + weight * residual(prefix, candidates,
                                               tables[route(category, user_id)])
        record_pinned_macro_validation_HR10(score)

select_by_macro_validation_HR10_with_prespecified_deterministic_tie_break()
# Tie break: lower residual weight, then unchanged BCE.
serialize_models_tables_routes_and_configuration_under_trial_directory()
emit_predictor_with_identical_scoring_and_routing()
# No all-user table rebuild; no claims of observed improvement before execution.

originality.positive: Combines recent directed association, explicit distinct-user support, and persistent excluded-fold routing in a focused SASRec extension.
originality.negative: Transition rules, smoothing, minimum support, recency weighting, and grouped estimation are established; the contribution is their controlled integration.

future_potential.positive: Provides an interpretable evidence channel and a clean foundation for later uncertainty-aware fusion if fixed-weight gains replicate.
future_potential.negative: Sparse coverage, heuristic thresholds, rare-item amplification, and uncertain links between transitions and practical usefulness may limit impact.

code_difficulty.positive: Keeps the SASRec architecture and uses sparse counts and deterministic score fusion.
code_difficulty.negative: User provenance, prefix-safe diagnostics, fold routing, efficient batched sparse lookup, and predictor-writer parity are substantial integration requirements.

related_work.title: TGCL4SR: Temporal Graph Contrastive Learning for Sequential Recommendation
contributions: Models temporal item-transition graphs, motivating complementary sequence and transition representations.
limitations: Does not establish effectiveness of this count-based residual on the pinned Amazon benchmark.

related_work.title: A Study of Smoothing Methods for Language Models Applied to Ad Hoc Information Retrieval
contributions: Provides the Dirichlet smoothing foundation for shrinking sparse conditional distributions toward a background prior.
limitations: Smoothing is not a support-reliability guarantee; single-row log-lift rankings remain determined by count divided by background probability before clipping.

related_work.title: Out-of-fold stacking reference supplied in the search results
contributions: Motivates constructing fusion features without the scored user's own training contribution.
limitations: User-grouped transition estimation is a proposed adaptation; refitting support on all users changes feature semantics and requires explicit validation.

related_work.title: gSASRec
contributions: Identifies sampled-BCE overconfidence and motivates an objective-focused control.
limitations: The proposed ordinary sampled CE control is distinct from generalized BCE and does not reproduce gSASRec.

related_work.title: GroupKFold documentation
contributions: Documents grouping that keeps every user's examples within one fold.
limitations: Grouping alone does not prevent future-prefix leakage or provide identities for anonymous training batches.

related_work.title: On Over-fitting in Model Selection and Subsequent Selection Bias in Performance Evaluation
contributions: Explains selection optimism from repeatedly optimizing validation performance.
limitations: A small fixed grid reduces opportunities for selection bias but does not eliminate it.

related_work.title: Statistical Significance Tests for Machine Translation Evaluation
contributions: Provides paired bootstrap methodology that can be adapted to user-level hit differences.
limitations: The proposed category-stratified adaptation measures conditional user-sampling uncertainty and does not correct adaptive selection.

related_work.title: On the Bias of Offline Evaluation Methods for Recommender Systems
contributions: Supports caution when interpreting rankings measured using sampled negative candidates.
limitations: The pinned evaluation remains required; its results cannot establish full-catalog or online performance.

related_work.title: Session-based recommendation comparison supplied in the search results
contributions: Motivates sequential-rule and neighborhood baselines as alternatives to more complex graph models.
limitations: Competitiveness on session datasets does not establish performance on these Amazon histories.

related_work.title: Temporal leakage study supplied in the search results
contributions: Motivates explicit prefix boundaries and careful separation of training information from held-out outcomes.
limitations: User exclusion does not enforce global chronological causality; benchmark splits must remain unchanged.
